title: Add sample Terraform snippets for budget + quota alerting (checklist-ready)
author: Cole Summers
description: Context: As part of the Guided Onboarding + First Production Launch checklist, we want customers to have an easy, copy/pasteable path to set spend guardrails and get alerted before hitting usage caps. This PR adds Terraform examples for (1) Redwood budgets (soft + hard caps) with threshold notifications and (2) quota + rate-limit alerting via exported metrics. The intent is to link these snippets from the checklist steps ("Set budgets/quotas" + "Configure alerts") and the docs IA updates. Scope: new examples under examples/budgets-alerts/ plus a small README refresh that clarifies how budgets behave (soft vs hard), recommended thresholds (80/95/100), and common onboarding gotchas (usage dashboard lag; alert delivery verification). Non-goals: no provider changes, no new resources; these examples assume existing redwood_* resources and are designed to run as-is with minimal variables. Testing: fmt + validate in CI; manual apply tested against a sandbox tenant (hosted) with email notification channel and a simulated usage spike.
commits: examples: add budget + alerts example scaffold
docs: clarify soft vs hard cap behavior and recommended thresholds
examples: add quota/rate-limit alert rules + variables
ci: run terraform fmt/validate for examples in pipeline
chore: address review feedback (naming, README copy, outputs)
review_conversation: Elliot Price (review): README is good, but can we make the checklist linkage explicit? E.g. call out that this is for the "Budgets & alerts" checklist step and include a short "What to do after apply" section (verify notification delivery, where to see it in Console).

Cole Summers (author): Yep. Added a top-of-file section in examples/budgets-alerts/README.md: "Checklist step: Configure budgets and alerts" + a short verification section (send test notification, confirm channel in Console).

Dev Patel (review): From Support perspective, we should be careful: customers often assume the budget cap blocks traffic immediately. Can we be explicit about the difference between soft budget (alert only) vs hard budget (request blocking) and warn about the ~N min lag in usage aggregation? This will reduce SUP-18510 style escalations.

Cole Summers (author): Good call. Updated wording to: soft=notifications only; hard=blocks after exceeded (subject to metering delay). Also added a note about dashboard/metering lag and to set thresholds with buffer (80/95) for first week.

Benji Okafor (review): Minor: variable names are a bit inconsistent (budget_limit_usd vs monthly_budget_usd). Suggest standardize and add a prefix to avoid collisions in copy/paste into existing stacks.
Cole Summers (author): Standardized to monthly_budget_usd and resource name prefix variable budget_name_prefix; updated outputs accordingly.
Connor O'Brien (review): CI: can we ensure terraform validate runs for the new example directory? Also, main workflow currently only checks root modules.
Cole Summers (author): Added a matrix entry for examples/budgets-alerts and runs fmt -check + validate. CI green now.
Elliot Price (approval): Approved. After this lands, I’ll link the example from the checklist docs page and the Console deep-link help text.
Dev Patel (approval): Approved. The lag + hard/soft clarification will help a lot.
release_notes: Added Terraform examples for configuring Redwood budgets (soft/hard caps) and threshold-based alerting.
Added Terraform examples for quota/rate-limit alerting based on exported usage metrics.
Updated CI to validate Terraform examples directories so snippets stay runnable.
